item: A robots.txt read refused by the kill switch, or cut off by it mid-request, is no longer cached as the host being unreachable
refs: R297; R293 delta read 2 (L2); R309 S3 (stated); PR #1562
summary: EthicalFetcher._get_robots caught every FetchError and requests error from its robots read as 'cannot determine robots, fail closed' and cached it (cause unreachable, one hour, failure counter, persisted sidecar line). The kill switch's own refusal is a FetchFailed and a switch engaging mid-request arrives as the socket guard's AirplaneModeError wrapped in a requests error, so a Stop pressed between fetch()'s first switch check and the robots read of a host whose verdict was not cached was recorded as the HOST being unreachable: measured with the real fetcher, the law tracker and one Stop, zero requests, RobotsUnavailable (unreachable), the law document stamped as checked, and the next pass (switch clear, fresh fetcher, same sidecar) stamped it again without asking the host; the collector filed it as ROBOTS_UNAVAILABLE. Now, when the kill switch is active, the except re-raises a FetchError as it is (it names the switch) and turns a requests error into the same FetchFailed with no cause chained (from None, the module's idiom; the sink sweep flagged the chain); nothing is cached or persisted, so the next fetch asks again. The decision is the switch, read after the failure, never a substring of the text; a real failure that coincides with a Stop is also not cached (one more request, the cautious direction); a robots answer that was received (a 200 then a Stop) is still cached; a FetchFailed whose words name the switch while the switch is clear is still the host's problem. declared_sitemaps (which documents that the switch makes it raise FetchFailed) now raises under a mid-read Stop instead of returning an empty list and caching; the collector files such a Stop as a fetch failure (offline) instead of ROBOTS_UNAVAILABLE. 11 tests in tests/test_robots_read_refused_by_switch.py cover both entry points (Stop pressed inside the per-host lock through fetch(), and a switch engaging mid-request) and the consequence through the real law tracker (the time given back, the next pass reads robots.txt again), plus controls for a real unreachable host, a real 403, a received answer (a 200, or a 403) then a Stop, a FetchError that is not the refusal re-raised unchanged under the switch, and a clear switch with a refusal-like text; 14 mutants caught by the eleven tests (the independent read's list: no guard fails 6, FetchError only 2, wrapped error only 4, cache and persist then raise 6, a bare raise of every error 4, relabelling every error under the switch 1, chaining the cause again 1, and seven more). Stated: the window is narrow and the entry lasted an hour, so the reach on a real corpus is not measured; the sentence is now a fifth literal in src/ingest/__init__.py (a named constant or a FetchFailed subclass is the sturdier follow-up); the law-tracker test depends on R293 (PR #1541) being on main. Routed with it and stated, not changed (WAL's deadline sweep S3): the bare count(*) in src/law/coverage.py (session.query(LawDocument).count()) cannot be stopped by the member deadline, but a filtered, stoppable count over the same table runs first in the same function and costs ten to thirty times more (warm, plain SQLite 3.45.1: 200,000 rows, bare 1.5 ms asked 0 times, filtered 46 ms stopped; 20,000 rows of 20 KB text, 0.3 ms against 3 ms); cold cache, SQLCipher and larger tables not measured. Found by the independent read and routed, not changed here (S1): the first-run preflight (src/monitoring/preflight.py, feed_preflight.py) files the switch's refusal as the host's robots verdict, writes the log that has_run_before() reads and overwrites robots_allowed with None; reproduced twice.
